column2: v2.0 — the planning layer, rebuilt text-first from the Hebrew: attribution from the superscriptions alone, the arc across the collections on counted and reproducible measures, the Greek's rival arrangement, the preaching traps, and the nine-sermon unit plan.

Eight macro-arguments the eleven runs jointly demonstrate. Proverbs is not an anthology that later acquired a frame but a designed book, and the design shows in three registers that do not depend on each other.
The original sweep: all eighteen units at proportional depth with a cross-passage synthesis. The seedbed the solo digs grew from.
The nine-sermon series plan, and the backbone of the opening survey sermon — a whole-book view with no single base text.

Sermon 2 backbone — v4, refreshed against the 18 September dig: the FCF moved from the voices to the position (v.5 → v.4), the חָכְמָה וּמוּסָר bracket made the spine, and the 1:3 → 2:9 handover confirmed audible in NIV84.

Sermon 3 backbone — v3, refreshed against the 18 September dig: out of both passivity and self-reliance into asking, on the כִּי of 2:6; the 1:3 → 2:9 handover made the third movement; the alphabet claim corrected and the NIV84 pulpit cost named.
The preamble bracketed by a single word-pair — ḥokmâ ûmûsār at verse 2 and again at verse 7 — and the bracket is the argument.
One sentence, twenty-two verses: three conditions, then, for, then, for, and two purpose-infinitives of rescue. The chapter that sets the agenda for chapters 3–7.
The frame entire. Chapter 2 announces a programme and chapters 3–7 execute it in order; ten lectures and five interludes, with Wisdom and Folly calling from the same height in chapter 9.

Solomon I, the umbrella pass (18 Sep 2026) — what the two halves jointly show: one deposit taught by two methods, welded by 16:25's reprint of 14:12; six measures moving at the seam and the speech rate holding; seven chains crossing it; and three New Testament citations, none of them from the Hebrew as the corpus holds it.

The Words of the Wise — a fresh text-first dig (23 Sep 2026): the book's most prohibitive and most directly addressed material (22 "do not"s and 22 grounds in 82 verses), the only setumah in Proverbs at 24:22 where the Greek inserts Agur, the unresolved crux at 22:20 that NIV84 settles as "thirty", and Romans 2:6 blended from the Greek of 24:12 and Psalm 61:13.

Hezekiah’s transcription — a fresh text-first dig (27 Sep 2026): three nested silences, all ending inside ch. 28; seven measures that split 25–27 from 28–29; the one da‘at in 138 verses, and it is about the poor; 3:7’s prohibition turned into four case studies welded to 25:2’s ḥāqar at 28:11; and Rom 12:20’s cut.

Agur and Lemuel’s mother — a fresh text-first dig (27 Sep 2026): 30:2–3 revokes 9:10 in its own words (da‘at qədōšîm stands in two verses of the Hebrew Bible); nəʾum haggeḇer four times in the canon — Balaam, David’s last words, Agur; the Greek reverses the confession and has neither Agur nor Lemuel; 30:4 is the one ascent-and-descent question John 3:13 matches; and the poor frame the unit at 30:14 and 31:9.

The closing acrostic — a fresh text-first dig (27 Sep 2026): five verified chains tie the poem to personified Wisdom (pənînîm, šaʿar, śḥq, ʾšr piel + tmk, mṣʾ); twenty-two verses contain one imperative and it is addressed to the reader, not to her; 27:2’s ban on self-praise is performed at 31:28–31; seven of the book’s chains end here and the motto closes in the adjective; and the Greek finds the ending hard enough to praise the husband instead.

Solomon I, first half — a fresh text-first dig (18 Sep 2026): the collection's boundaries shown to be Masoretic (Swete has no superscription at 10:1, and MT 15:33 stands at Swete 16:4), the contrast engine measured four ways, and 1 Peter 4 quoting the collection twice — once following the Hebrew, once the Greek.

Solomon I, second half — a fresh text-first dig (18 Sep 2026): the antithesis engine switched off (5.2%, three chapters at zero), the man/YHWH couplet counted in seven sentences, the book's longest divine-name run straddling the 15:33/16:1 seam, and 2 Cor 9:7 resting on a Greek plus at 22:8 with no Hebrew behind it.
Ansberry’s collection scheme for Proverbs 10–29 tested against the text before the sweeps began. It stands — with three corrections and one caution.
Thirty-three manual library returns graded against the open questions of the 1:1–7, Proverbs 2 and 1:8–9:18 reports. The status board near the top overrides every other status statement.
Twenty answers audited: eleven adopted as given, six with qualification, three rejected — including one claim the Hebrew text refutes outright.

The whole book read against the Greek at last. Forty-eight lettered pluses and twenty-four Hebrew verses with no Greek counterpart — concentrated, not scattered: eighteen in the frame, none at all in 30–31.

The forest, for use while working in the wood. A one-page spine of the book’s argument, then one card per sermon — the strongest finding, the Big Question’s answer, the Christ line and the trap. Compression only; no new findings.
Sermon 4 backbone — v2 on the whole frame (1:1–9:18): the handover of voice from father to Wisdom, the three escalating calls, 1:28 answered at 8:17, and the four identical words at 9:4 and 9:16.

Sermon 5 backbone — v2 on the three September runs: the world sorted, the crest, the auditor disqualified — three movements on the transmitted paragraphs, welded by 16:25's reprint of 14:12, landing on 20:9 and answered in its own vocabulary at 1 John 1:7.

Sermon 6 backbone — v2 on the 23 September dig: wisdom from an unnamed collective, re-founded on trust at 22:19 before a single prohibition, and tested at the gate, the boundary stone and the excuse of 24:12. Four movements on the transmitted paragraphs; highest moralism risk in the series, with the text's own guard named.

Sermon 7 backbone, v2 (27 Sep 2026), rebuilt on the fresh whole-unit dig — the withheld name as the collection’s method, 26:12 and 28:11 as trapdoors under the sermon the material invites, and the verdict that has to come from outside (27:2). Four movements; NIV84 pulpit notes on 28:26 and 29:7.

Sermon 8 backbone, v2 (27 Sep 2026), rebuilt on the fresh dig — Agur revokes 9:10 in its own words, 30:4’s question is held open until the end of movement 3, and the unit’s frame runs from the poor devoured (30:14) to the poor defended (31:9). Four movements; NIV84 pulpit notes on 30:7 and 31:8, both on a movement’s hinge.
Sermon 9 backbone, closing the series — one imperative in twenty-two verses, it is the book’s last word, and it is addressed to the observer: recognise wisdom in another and say so publicly.
